findings.evidence: The WebView element in activity_main.xml (line 9) is the standard Capacitor shell that renders the app's own React UI bundled in dist/. It does not access or collect the user's external web browsing history. The loadUrl pattern was not found in index-PqeuXPtB.js (false positive grep match). No web browsing history data collection logic exists in the codebase.
findings.recommendation: No action needed. WebView is used solely as the app rendering engine (Capacitor). This data type is not collected.

findings.evidence: Email is collected in three paths: (1) user-provided email during Supabase Auth sign-up/sign-in via index-BMHFFNQZ.js (supabase-js auth client sends email to Supabase Auth endpoint); (2) Google OAuth callback at api/auth/callback.js:34 (tokens.email passed to salvarToken()); (3) stored server-side via api/db.js:43-46 in user_tokens table. All paths are user-initiated (user chooses to sign up or connect Gmail). Destination is the developer's own Supabase/PostgreSQL backend (first party).
findings.recommendation: Declare email collection in Play Store Data Safety form under 'App functionality' with user-initiated flag. No prominent in-app disclosure required since collection is user-initiated.

findings.evidence: Full email content (subject, body, recipient, attachment) is transmitted when the user composes and sends an email via api/enviar.js:50 (transporter.sendMail()). The user provides all fields (destinatario, assunto, corpoHtml, pdfBase64) via POST request. The email is relayed through the developer's Vercel server to Gmail API (third-party delivery service chosen by the user). This is a manual sharing action by the user.
findings.recommendation: Policy exempt (manual sharing). No disclosure or Play Store declaration needed. User explicitly triggers the send action with full knowledge of the content being transmitted.
